The very last thing that I did at the company was sit in a group call watching the stream of the awards show at BIG Festival at Gamescom Latam, which aired at the end of the day on Friday of my last week. We were up for best gameplay, which it won--our only win (in my area!): talk about whiplash.

Today is the 2 year anniversary of Pacific Drive's release. I'm also in the thick of refining my GDC talk about it, which I was meant to give last year before I needed emergency surgery, so it's been on my mind a lot lately. Here's a long 🧵.

If you'll be at GDC: schedule.gdconf.com/session/paci...

Once home, my schedule worsened: I was the interim producer on top of everything else, staying up to 5am EST. We also had ~8 deliverables over the next month--it was meant to be the run up to release--including me flying to Cologne for Gamescom for 3 days of double- and triple-booked press previews.

But it didn't quite go as planned: the abuse that I had subjected my body to over the course of the project came home to roost as I got sick in January of 2025, and ended up needing emergency surgery. With the health challenges before surgery and recovery after, I couldn't attend GDC anymore.

This also meant that I would miss the IGF and GDCA awards ceremony: we were nominated for 1 award in each, with the IGF nom being for design. I was, and am, devastated to have missed that event. For me, IGF is the awards that recognizes the most exciting work happening.

That made it a bittersweet night, continuing what became a trend of a rollercoaster awards season for me, personally. We lost to Balatro, which is hard to get mad about--that game is excellent, and a worthy winner. I headed back to my hermit hole and resumed working on my GDC talk.

July 2024: I left Ironwood, hoping to get some much needed rest and recovery from severe burnout. Instead, I had to move out of my apt in NYC within the next 2 months due to our lease not being renewed. I dispatched for my parents' vacation house as a temporary home, and got to work on my GDC talk.

Now I'm recovered, and once again working on the GDC talk that I was meant to give a year ago. It feels like it's been a very long time since the game came out and also like I am stuck in time, with barely a minute elapsing. I am hoping that giving this presentation will provide some closure for me.
